candidate.title: SHAPE-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina SHAPE-Seq schematic depicts the barcoded, in vitro folded RNA implementation: RNA to Barcoded RNA to 1M7 reaction to two separate reverse-transcription examples to RNA hydrolysis and cDNA. SHAPE-Seq is the sole target; the expanded far-left title is its name, not another method. The upper and lower routes illustrate different modification/extension endpoints, not alternative named protocols or control samples. The collection heading and caption ('A schematic overview of SHAPE-Seq.') match the assigned target. The drawing ends at cDNA; downstream library completion, deep sequencing and structural inference are not drawn and are described here only to interpret the readout. In-cell SHAPE-Seq and other bibliography applications do not expand this scope. Collection reference 150 (Watters et al., Methods, 2016, Characterizing RNA structures in vitro and in vivo with selective 2’-hydroxyl acylation analyzed by primer extension sequencing) is a catalogue-only citation without a registered publication source; it supplies no verified implementation evidence. Primary scientific content supplied is abstract-only; catalogue descriptions are secondary evidence. The readout supports structural inference under the probed in vitro conditions, with background transcriptase drop-off requiring controls; it does not directly image a complete RNA fold.

operations.label: 1M7 reaction
operations.description: Treats folded barcoded RNA with 1M7, yielding RNA marked at different sites. The two outputs preserve the upper-loop and side-bulge examples shown in the drawing; they are example molecular outcomes of the same treatment, not named alternative assays or treated/untreated controls.
operations.mechanism: SHAPE chemistry selectively acylates RNA 2'-hydroxyl groups. The depicted red modifications create reverse-transcription blocks; no detailed reaction structure is supplied by the schematic.
operations.information_effect: Transfers information about the probed RNA structure into the positions of chemical modifications that can be interrogated by primer extension. The schematic is not a complete inventory of all possible reaction outcomes.

The Lucks abstract supports the SHAPE chemistry and multiplexed primer-extension sequencing association without supplying the complete protocol.
